## Summary

The U.S. Senate confirmed Herschel Walker on Tuesday to serve as the United States' next ambassador to the Bahamas, filling a position that has been vacant for nearly 15 years. Walker was one of more than 100 nominees confirmed in a single vote, after Republican lawmakers changed Senate rules to allow quicker confirmation of President Donald Trump's nominees.

Walker, 63, ran as a Republican for the U.S. Senate in Georgia in 2022, losing narrowly to Democrat Raphael Warnock. He was nominated for the ambassadorship in December by then-President-elect Donald Trump, a longtime associate. Walker was confirmed by the US Senate on October 7, and sworn in at the White House on October 17.
